Matchup Lab

Matchup Lab

NBA.com season matchup data (who guarded whom, 151,960 pairs) combined with our play-by-play profiles, xFG and lineup on/off. 2025–26 regular season. Roles are clustered from NBA playtype frequencies, height, on-ball time and shot zones. All results labeled PROXY.

Every defender with 800+ partial possessions of matchups. Difficulty = average scoring load (points per 100 on-court possessions) of the players he guarded, weighted by time. Versatility = how evenly his time spread over the 9 offensive roles (0 = one role, 1 = all equally). Pts saved = points his matchups scored below what those same players scored against everyone else, per 100 partial possessions. Compare it within the same role: rim bigs score low by construction because they get credited at the rim. Click a header to sort.

Every attacker × defender pair from NBA.com's season matchup data (pairs with 2+ partial possessions). Expected = what the attacker scores per possession against every other defender, times the time in this pair. Confidence follows partial possessions: 300+ very good, 150+ good, 60+ some, 25+ poor. These are direct-credit numbers, so a defender can be charged for switches and rotations (see Matchup vs help). Use them to explore, not to award badges.

defending

Point-of-attack trust. Each team's lead creators = the top 2 by usage on every team (60 players, 800+ on-court possessions). For each defense, we look at who it put on those players and for how long. That's a coaching decision, measured in time guarded, so it isn't affected by which defender gets charged for shots. Team load share = his share of his team's matchup time on opposing lead creators. Primary on = how many of those creators he guarded more than any teammate. Focus = share of his own matchup time spent on lead creators, compared league-wide (how much of a POA specialist he is).

Each team's point-of-attack defender

Confidence for "this is the team's POA": very good = 600+ possessions on lead creators, a lead of 8+ points of share over the next teammate, and primary on 30%+ of creators faced; good = 400+ and 5+ lead; some = 200+ and 2+ lead; otherwise poor (the job is shared).

Who each team put on a lead creator

Option stoppers: most matchups vs the 1st/2nd option on the floor

For each possession, the offense's 1st and 2nd options = its two highest-usage players on the floor. Each defender's matchup time is split by how often the player he guarded was a 1st or 2nd option. Share = how much of his own guarding time went to them. The 30 highlighted defenders (half or more of their time on top options, most volume) are the "option stoppers" used in the Vs option stoppers tab.

Forced vs chosen assignments

Uses real body data: height and weight (NBA.com) and wingspan (draft combine, 363 players). For every possession and every attacker, the similar-build defenders on the floor are those within a combined distance of 1.5, where 3 inches of height, 35 lb of weight or 4 inches of wingspan each count as 1 (combined like a straight-line distance). If only one is on the floor, the assignment is forced (the only big has to take Jokić). If several are, the coach chose. Only time on the offense's 1st and 2nd options counts.

Forced share = his top-option time where he was the only similar-size defender. Off-build share = top-option time on players outside his build range (always a choice). Trust index = his top-option time ÷ what he'd get by an even split with similar-size teammates (1.0 = fair share). Labels: Forced = forced share 50%+. Trusted = trust 1.25+ and mostly chosen. Hidden = trust 0.7 or less and mostly chosen. Shared = in between. Small guards who take bigger wings and bigs who switch onto guards score high on trust. That's real, but it's "chosen across sizes," not necessarily "best defender."

Check against BBall Index matchup difficulty

BBall Index's 2025-26 76ers percentiles (from your screenshots) vs ours. Rank agreement: usage-weighted difficulty 0.98, option share 0.96, points-load 0.90. Their top 5 (Dort, Daniels, Wells, Castle, Okoro) are all in our top 6. Kris Dunn: BBall Index 98%, ours 98% (usage-weighted).

League POA defenders

Defenders with 300+ possessions on lead creators. "Pts vs expected" and "FG% saved" are on those assignments only. Read FG% saved as the more trustworthy of the two (see Matchup vs help).

Direct defense by defender

Built only from the matchup metrics that agree with on/off: FG% saved on his own man (60%) and help blocks (40%), each ranked within role and shrunk for sample size. FGA denial and points saved are shown for contrast. They mostly measure where tracking credit lands, not stops. Funnel = his man shoots much less against him (top ~16% in role) while the team allows more with him on (on/off surprise worse than +0.01): likely getting beaten and the shot being credited to a helper.

Misses don't carry an assist tag, so assisted attempts are estimated: each shot type and zone (catch-and-shoot jumper, pull-up, cut, alley-oop, putback…) gets the assisted rate seen on makes, then that probability is applied to every attempt. Checked against the makes we do know: the predicted vs actual assisted share by player correlates at r = (average miss points). Receiver shotmaking = points minus league-adjusted xFG points per likely-assisted attempt, shrunk by 40 attempts. Receiver value = that surplus per 100 of his on-court possessions (volume × efficiency).
